jb2.py.summary: Reformat every JSON file below the current directory with two-space indentation.
details: Parses each file, writes it back through :func:`json.dump` (``ensure_ascii`` off) and reports the size change per file plus the total freed, using a worker pool.

jg.py.summary: Empty every repository below the current directory, keeping only its ``.git`` folder.
details: For each ``.git`` directory found it removes all sibling files and folders, leaving a clean checkout directory with the history in place. This is destructive: run it from the tree you want to strip and keep a backup.
jg.py.notes: Irreversible — it deletes the working tree of every repository below the current directory.

joinlines.py.summary: Join all non-empty lines of a file into a single line.
details: Strips the line endings, concatenates the remaining text and appends one final newline, rewriting the file in place.

justwhl.py.summary: Reduce each sub-directory of the current directory to its single ``.whl`` file.
details: Looks for a wheel in the sub-directory or its ``dist/`` folder, moves it up when needed and deletes every other file and folder in that sub-directory, leaving one wheel per project. Sub-directories without a wheel are skipped.
justwhl.py.notes: Deletes the build leftovers of each sub-directory, so review the tree before running it.

l2c.py.summary: Copy one line of a file to the Termux clipboard.
details: Reads the requested (zero-based) line, strips the surrounding whitespace and feeds it to ``termux-clipboard-set``.

last5minutes.py.summary: Cut the last five minutes out of an audio file.
details: Opens the audio with moviepy, takes the final 230 seconds and writes them to ``last_5_minutes.mp3`` at 320 kbit/s.

lastncommits.py.summary: List the files that were added during the last N commits.
details: Runs ``git log -n N --name-status --diff-filter=A`` in the current repository, skips symlinks and prints the paths of the created files.

licr.py.summary: Empty the license files below the current directory.
details: Finds files whose name starts with ``license`` and whose extension is ``.md``, ``.txt``, ``.rst`` or absent, prints them and truncates each one to zero bytes.
licr.py.notes: Destructive by design: the license texts are emptied in place.

list_files_starting_with.py.summary: List the entries of the current directory whose name starts with a prefix.
details: Prints the matching names, ignoring symbolic links; the prefix is read from the first argument.

lkk.py.summary: List the files in the current directory whose name contains a substring.
details: Prints the matching names sorted alphabetically, marking symlinks with their target; ``-s`` also includes symlinks (they are skipped by default).

ll.py.summary: Print an ``ls``-style listing of the current directory with sizes and colours.
details: Shows the modification time, size (directories report their total) and name of every entry, colourising symlinks differently and sorting by size (``-r`` reverses the order).

loname.py.summary: Normalize the file names of the current directory to lowercase snake style.
details: Lower-cases the stem, drops punctuation other than ``_``/``-``, replaces spaces with underscores, collapses repeats and lower-cases the extension, keeping the existing files under a unique name when a rename would collide.

lowerer.py.summary: Lower-case the whole content of a text file.
details: Reads the file as UTF-8, applies :meth:`str.lower` to the entire text and writes it back in place.

ltxt.py.summary: Count the unique non-blank lines of text files, per extension.
details: Walks the given paths (or the current directory), skips binaries by extension and counts the stripped lines that appear more than once, grouping the counts per file extension. ``--pool-method`` selects how the counting jobs are spread over the worker pool.
